questions.question: You point at a part while the agent is mid-build. What should happen?
options: Mark it, tell the agent nothing
questions.answer: Queue it as context

questions.question: When the model receives a part you pointed at, how much should it be told about that part?
questions.answer: Everything already measured

questions.question: Should the model also get a picture of what you pointed at, or only the numbers?
questions.answer: Both — numbers plus a crop

questions.question: How do you pick a part in the live view?
questions.answer: Click, and drag to circle
questions.notes: hover shows the name without committing — that is the 'find things' path

questions.question: Right now, dragging anywhere in the view turns the camera. If picking also uses drag, how should the two share it?
options: A Point mode you switch into
Drag on a part points, drag on empty space orbits
Hold a modifier key to point
questions.answer: A Point mode you switch into

questions.question: Parts overlap on screen constantly. When you point where several stack up, what do you get?
options: The nearest, with a way to cycle deeper
A small list of everything under the cursor
questions.answer: The nearest one

questions.question: You've picked a part. Where do you type the instruction that goes with it?
options: The existing conversation box, with the part attached
A small box that opens beside the part
questions.answer: A small box that opens beside the part
questions.notes: NOT the recommendation. The user chose annotation-in-place over the existing composer — type where you are looking. Consequence: a new floating composer anchored to the picked part's screen position, and it must not obscure the geometry being discussed.

questions.question: Where should the picture the model sees actually come from?
options: A crop of your live view
A fresh Blender render of that part
questions.answer: A crop of your live view

questions.question: Should you be able to attach a reference image of your own?
options: Yes — drag or paste one in
questions.answer: Yes — drag or paste one in

questions.question: You mark a part as important so the model pays more attention to it. What does "important" actually mean to the model?
options: A standing instruction it re-reads every turn
A rule it is not allowed to break
A one-off nudge on the next action
questions.answer: A standing instruction it re-reads every turn
questions.notes: This is the decisive difference from a redirect: notes are drained and cleared on delivery (reporting.py:187-188); focus must NOT be, or it is forgotten by the third action.

questions.question: How long should a part stay marked as important?
options: Until the agent has worked on that part
questions.answer: Until you clear it

questions.question: Should you be able to say how important — or is a part simply marked or not?
options: A number you set per part
questions.answer: Simply marked

questions.question: How should a part YOU marked look different from the agent's change-highlight?
options: A list in the panel, nothing in the 3D view
questions.answer: A persistent coloured outline
questions.notes: Must not reuse viewport state.highlighted — applyHighlight clears every previous id on each HIGHLIGHT, which would wipe the operator's marks every time the agent touched anything.

questions.question: Which edits should you be able to make yourself, without asking the model?
questions.answer: Move, rotate, scale; Delete and duplicate; Hide and show; Rename, and change material
questions.notes: All four picked — full scope. None of these exists today: all 33 replayable operation kinds are construction or repair.

questions.question: How do you actually drive a move or a rotate?
options: Drag handles in the view, with numbers beside them
questions.answer: Drag handles in the view, with numbers beside them

questions.question: When you drag a part, should it snap?
options: Snap to a grid, and you can turn it off
Snap to nearby parts — faces and edges
questions.answer: Snap to a grid, and you can turn it off

questions.question: The agent holds a single write lock. You grab a part and drag it while the agent is mid-action. Who wins?
options: You do — your edit goes in as soon as its action finishes
You do, immediately — the agent is paused for you
You have to press Pause first
questions.answer: You have to press Pause first
questions.notes: NOT the recommendation, and the most conservative option. Consequence: the manual edit path never contends for the write lock at all — it is only reachable while the run is paused, which removes the entire class of two-writer races. Q-20 covers making that legible rather than mysterious.

questions.question: Should the agent be told when you move something yourself?
questions.answer: Yes, always

questions.question: Your manual edits and the agent's edits both change the scene. Should undo treat them the same?
questions.answer: One shared history
questions.notes: This is why manual edits must be real logged Operations rather than direct engine writes — replay, checkpoints and roll-back-N come for free, and diverging timelines become impossible.

questions.question: You pick a part while the run is going and reach for the move handle — what do you get?
options: Handles greyed out, with a Pause button right there
Picking up a handle pauses the build for you
No handles at all until you pause
questions.answer: Handles greyed out, with a Pause button right there

questions.question: You drag a part somewhere that breaks something. What does the product do?
options: Lets you, then tells you what broke
Warns you while you drag, before you let go
questions.answer: Lets you, then tells you what broke

questions.question: The connection drops while you have a part picked and half-moved. What should you see?
options: The move reverts, and it says so
It holds your position and re-sends on reconnect
questions.answer: The move reverts, and it says so

questions.question: How big should the crop sent to the model be?
questions.answer: Full — up to 1024px
questions.notes: NOT the recommendation — the user chose detail over per-point cost. 1024 is also downscale_image's own documented default max_edge, so the two now agree rather than one overriding the other.

questions.question: Should you be able to point at parts using only the keyboard?
options: Yes — tab through parts, space to pick
Keyboard for picking, mouse for dragging
questions.answer: Yes — tab through parts, space to pick

questions.question: Which of these matters most for the first version to feel right?
options: The model visibly acting on what you pointed at
The editing tools feeling like a real editor
questions.answer: Pointing feeling instant and exact
questions.notes: Sets the priority order for the build: pixel-exact picking is unit 1 and gets the most care. It is also why picking reads an id buffer written by the rasterizer rather than casting a ray — exact by construction, not approximately right.
